unit.sep: Compare instrument evidence,distinguish observation from supplied function knowledge,construct models and link levels of organisation.
unit.careers: Illustrative microscopy,biological modelling and source-evidence practices;no clinical diagnosis or professional laboratory qualification.
unit.focus: Conventional light/electron microscopy,accurately captioned real plant/animal images,component functions,models and levels of organisation with honest visibility/action limits.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional poster labels every visible grain as an organelle and rejects a root cell as plant because no chloroplast is visible.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Onion-root and cheek light images,leaf and cardiac TEMsections,a fresh root TEM,source scale bars,generalised models and linked concept maps.
unit.drivingQuestion: What can a cell image establish,and how do its structures support an organism? KICD: What makes up an organism?
unit.storylineThread: Instrument choice/resolution → plant light → animal light → plant TEM → animal TEM → shared functions → model comparison → organisation → construction → digital source → audit → independent evidence.
unit.coreCompetencies:
Creativity and Imagination: as the learner constructs a model of plant and animal cells as seen under the electron microscope.
Digital literacy: as the learner searches for information from the internet on the structure of a cell as seen under the electron microscope.
Learning to learn: as the learner reflects on the project work and adjusts appropriately.
unit.values:
Respect: as the learner considers others’ opinion while working on practical activities in groups such as construction of models.
Social justice: as the learner seeks equity, equality and gender consideration in distribution of learning resources such as sharing of materials for making cell models.
unit.pcis:
Environmental conservation: as the learner manages wastes responsibly to avoid pollution while preparing plant and animal cell models.
Safety and security; as the learner observes safety precautions when preparing the models.
unit.content: Types of microscopes; Differences between light and electron microscopes.; Cell structure and functions; Levels of cell organisation

assessment.instructions: Lesson12,40minutes:4procedure,12sections1–2,16section3andtheconceptmapspartofsection4,4section4benefit/limit,4checking/collection. Work independently with CL13andCL14only. Captions/source labels are openly supplied,not a blind identification test. The plant image is withheld from teaching materials;the animal source is intentionally reused. No teaching cards,models,hints or peer discussion. Written interpretation does not certify physical construction or actual online research actions.

sections.title: 1. Microscope choice and evidence
sections.prompt: Compare conventional light microscopy withTEMin signal,preparation/living-state limits and resolving detail. Choose a method for observing living movement and one for prepared internal ultrastructure;state whatSEMadds. Explain why digital zoom alone does not resolve originally merged features.
sections.exemplar: Light uses visible light/lenses and can observe living or prepared specimens depending on method;conventional TEMuses electrons through prepared nonliving thin sections for finer internal detail. Light suits living movement,TEMinternal ultrastructure,SEMpreparedsurface information. Digital enlargement changes display size,not information absent from the original resolution. Do not overstate this school comparison as covering every specialised research technique.

sections.title: 2. Supported image observations and comparison limits
sections.prompt: Using CL13andCL14,cite two supported structural observations from each and one justified not-resolved/not-in-frame statement for each. Explain why root tissue need not show leaf chloroplasts and why the animal field is not a complete generic cell. Explain how a light image and aTEMmaydiffer,and give one reason these different tissues are not a controlled same-cell comparison.
sections.exemplar: Plantrootsection supports walls/enclosed sections/nuclear material;animalcardiacfield supports nuclear/nucleolar and mitochondrial/cristae features. Accept cautious correctly located alternatives,not forced ambiguous vesicle labels. Neither view establishes a complete inventory or resolved full membrane bilayer;animalfullcell/complete nucleus extend outside frame. Rootnonphotosynthetic context differs from leaf;animal tissue is specialised. TEMcanresolvefinerpreparedinternal detail,but tissue,contrast,stain andsectionplane also differ from light samples;not all visible differences are caused only by instrument.

sections.title: 3. Component functions and model conditions
sections.prompt: Explain functions of nucleus,plasma membrane,ribosomes andmitochondria. Add two features/functions expected in a generalised photosynthetic plant model and explain why their model presence does not force visibility in every plant sample. Distinguish one observed structure from its supplied/known biological function.

sections.title: 4. Organisation,basic unit and evidence limits
sections.prompt: Draw labelled relationship maps from cardiac muscle cell to mouse and from a specified root cell/tissue to onion plant,including tissue,organ and organ system.
